(edge != 0) {470        return edge - 1;471    }472    to: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, kayan_table_at(w, from)*.signature & ~kayan_bit(id));473    kayan_table_at(w, from)*.remove_edges[id] = to + 1;474    kayan_table_at(w, to)*.add_edges[id] = from + 1;475    return to;476}477 478// Move a live entity to table `to_index`. Components both tables have are479// copied, byte for byte; components only the new table has start zeroed;480// components only the old table has are dropped with its old row.481kayan_move: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, to_index: u32) -> void = {482    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));483    from_index: u32 = slot*.table;484    if (from_index == to_index) {485        return;486    }487    from_row: u64 = cast(slot*.row, u64);488    from: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, from_index);489    to: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, to_index);490    to_row: u64 = kayan_table_add_row(w, to, e);491    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {492        fc: option<*kayan_column in level> = from*.columns[id];493        tc: option<*kayan_column in level> = to*.columns[id];494        if (fc && tc) {495            dst: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(tc, to_row);496            src: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(fc, from_row);497            for (i: u64 = 0; i < dst.length; i += 1) {498                dst[i] = src[i];499            }500        }501    }502    kayan_table_remove_row(w, from, from_row);503    slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));504    slot*.table = to_index;505    slot*.row = cast(to_row, u32);506}507 508// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------509// The byte layer, for tools510// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------511 512// e's component `id` as its bytes: an empty slice if e is dead or has no such513// component. The typed layer is for game code, which knows its types; this is514// for tools that work from reflect records instead.515kayan_get_bytes: proc(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32) -> []u8 in level = {516    none: []u8 in level = {};517    if (!kayan_alive(w, e) || id >= w*.component_count) {518        return none;519    }520    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));521    table: u32 = slot*.table;522    row: u32 = slot*.row;523    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, table);524    c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];525    if (!c) {526        return none;527    }528    return kayan_column_bytes(c, cast(row, u64));529}530 531// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------532// The typed layer533// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------534 535// e's T, or null if e is dead or has no T. Handle, slot, table, row, typed536// view: the same path as 1.4's get_position, for any component. `option<*T>` says the537// null is possible, so the caller tests before it reads. The pointer is good538// until the next structural change, so use it now and keep the handle.539kayan_get: proc<T>(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> option<*T in level> = {540    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {541        return null;542    }543    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));544    table: u32 = slot*.table;545    row: u32 = slot*.row;546    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, table);547    if (!kayan_table_has(t, kayan_id_of<T>())) {548        return null;549    }550    rows: []T in level = kayan_slice<T>(t);551    return rows[cast(row, u64)]&;552}553 554kayan_has: proc<T>(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {555    return (kayan_signature(w, e) & kayan_mask_of<T>()) != 0;556}557 558// Write e's T. It must already have one: giving an entity a component it does559// not have changes its table, which is 2.6.560kayan_set: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {561    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {562        return kayan_status.dead;563    }564    p: option<*T> = kayan_get<T>(w, e);565    if (!p) {566        return kayan_status.missing;567    }568    p* = value;569    return kayan_status.ok;570}571 572// Give e a T. If it already has one, this is kayan_set; if not, it moves to573// the table with T and then sets it.574kayan_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {575    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {576        return kayan_status.dead;577    }578    if (!kayan_has<T>(w, e)) {579        from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.table;580        kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_with(w, from, kayan_id_of<T>()));581    }582    return kayan_set<T>(w, e, value);583}584 585// Take e's T away, moving it to the table without T.586kayan_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {587    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {588        return kayan_status.dead;589    }590    if (!kayan_has<T>(w, e)) {591        return kayan_status.missing;592    }593    from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.table;594    kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_without(w, from, kayan_id_of<T>()));595    return kayan_status.ok;596}597 598// The invariant, over every table: each row belongs to a live entity whose599// slot points back at that table and row, and the rows of all tables add up to600// the live count.601kayan_verify: proc(w: *const kayan_world) -> u64 = {602    problems: u64 = 0;603    rows: u64 = 0;604    for (ti: u64 = 0; ti < w*.tables*.length; ti += 1) {605        t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32));606        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t*.count; row += 1) {607            // Taken row by row: kayan_alive takes the world, and the checker608            // does not know that it leaves the rows where they are.609            es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(t);610            e: kayan_entity = es[row];611            if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {612                printfmt("kayan_verify: table {} row {} holds dead entity {}:{}\n", ti, row, e.index, e.generation);613                problems += 1;614                continue;615            }616            slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));617            if (cast(slot*.table, u64) != ti || cast(slot*.row, u64) != row) {618                printfmt("kayan_verify: {}:{} is in table {} row {}, its slot says table {} row {}\n",619                    e.index, e.generation, ti, row, slot*.table, slot*.row);620                problems += 1;621            }622        }623        rows += t*.count;624    }625    if (rows != w*.live) {626        printfmt("kayan_verify: {} rows in tables, {} live entities\n", rows, w*.live);627        problems += 1;628    }629    return problems;630}631 632kayan_print_signature: proc(w: *const kayan_world, signature: u64) -> void = {633    printfmt("{");634    first: b32 = true;635    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {636        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {637            if (!first) {638                printfmt(" ");639            }640            printfmt("{}", kayan_info(w, id)*.name);641            first = false;642        }643    }644    printfmt("}");645}646 647kayan_print_table: proc(w: *const kayan_world, ti: u32) -> void = {648    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, ti);649    printfmt("    table {} ", ti);650    kayan_print_signature(w, t*.signature);651    printfmt(":");652    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(t);653    for (row: u64 = 0; row < es.length; row += 1) {654        e: kayan_entity = es[row];655        printfmt(" {}:{}", e.index, e.generation);656    }657    printfmt("\n");658}659 660kayan_print_tables: proc(w: *const kayan_world) -> void = {661    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w*.tables*.length, u32); ti += 1) {662        kayan_print_table(w, ti);663    }664}665 666// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------667// The inspector: reflect records, no component types668// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------669 670kayan_indent: proc(depth: u32) -> void = {671    for (i: u32 = 0; i < depth; i += 1) {672        printfmt("    ");673    }674}675 676// One value of a builtin type, read from its bytes by its type's name. The677// bytes may sit at any address, so the read is a copy into a local: this is the678// inspector's one unsafe block.679kayan_print_builtin: proc(type_name: ^const char, at: []const u8) -> void = {680    if (at.length < 4) {681        printfmt("<{} bytes>", at.length);682        return;683    }684    unsafe {685        if (reflect_cstr_equal(type_name, "f32")) {686            f: f32 = 0.0;687            memcpy(f&, at.data, 4);688            printfmt("{:.2}", cast(f, f64));689        } else if (reflect_cstr_equal(type_name, "u32")) {690            u: u32 = 0;691            memcpy(u&, at.data, 4);692            printfmt("{}", u);693        } else if (reflect_cstr_equal(type_name, "i32")) {694            i: i32 = 0;695            memcpy(i&, at.data, 4);696            printfmt("{}", i);697        } else {698            printfmt("<{}>", type_name);699        }700    }701}702 703// Every field of a struct whose bytes are `base`, nested structs indented704// under their field. A field's bytes are cut from `base` by its offset and705// size, both from the reflect record.706kayan_print_fields: proc(type: *const reflect, base: []const u8, depth: u32) -> void = {707    for (i: u64 = 0; i < type*.count; i += 1) {708        f: option<*const reflect_field> = reflect_field_at(type, i);709        if (!f) {710            continue;711        }712        if (reflect_field_has_attr(f, "hidden")) {713            continue;714        }715        at: []const u8 = base[f*.offset..f*.offset + f*.size];716        kayan_indent(depth);717        printfmt("{}:", f*.name);718        info: option<*const reflect> = reflect_field_info(f);719        if (info && info*.kind == reflect_kind_struct) {720            printfmt("\n");721            kayan_print_fields(info, at, depth + 1);722        } else {723            printfmt(" ");724            kayan_print_builtin(f*.type, at);725            printfmt("\n");726        }727    }728}729 730kayan_inspect: proc(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {731    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {732        printfmt("{}:{} (dead)\n", e.index, e.generation);733        return;734    }735    printfmt("{}:{} ", e.index, e.generation);736    signature: u64 = kayan_signature(w, e);737    kayan_print_signature(w, signature);738    printfmt("\n");739    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {740        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {741            info: *const reflect in permanent = kayan_info(w, id);742            printfmt("    {}\n", info*.name);743            bytes: []u8 = kayan_get_bytes(w, e, id);744            kayan_print_fields(info, bytes, 2);745        }746    }747}748 749// Every table: rows in use out of room, and per column its row size and its750// bytes in use out of bytes allocated. The memory a table holds and does not751// use is the cost of doubling on growth.752kayan_print_layout: proc(w: *const kayan_world) -> void = {753    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w*.tables*.length, u32); ti += 1) {754        t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, ti);755        printfmt("table {} ", ti);756        kayan_print_signature(w, t*.signature);757        printfmt(": {} rows, room for {}\n", cast(t*.count, u32), cast(t*.capacity, u32));758        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {759            c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];760            if (c) {761                size: u64 = c*.size;762                printfmt("    {:-9} {:2} bytes a row, {:4} of {:4} bytes in use\n", kayan_info(w, id)*.name, cast(size, u32),763                    cast(size * t*.count, u32), cast(size * t*.capacity, u32));764            }765        }766    }767}768 769// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------770// Queries771// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------772 773// The tables a system runs over: every table whose signature has all of `all`774// and none of `none`, kept by index. Tables are only ever added, at the end of775// w.tables, so the query remembers how many it has checked and, brought up to776// date, looks at the new ones only.777kayan_query: struct = {778    all: u64;779    none: u64;780    tables: *vec<u32> in level;781    checked: u64;782}783 784// The list of matched tables lives in the world's region, so a query says785// which region it is made in.786kayan_query_init: proc(r: region level, all: u64, none: u64) -> kayan_query = {787    return { .all = all, .none = none, .tables = vec<u32>make(r, 4) };788}789 790kayan_matches: proc(signature: u64, all: u64, none: u64) -> b32 = {791    return (signature & all) == all && (signature & none) == 0;792}793 794// Check the tables made since the query last looked. With none new, this is795// one comparison, so call it before every walk.796kayan_query_update: proc(w: *const kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {797    for (ti: u64 = q*.checked; ti < w*.tables*.length; ti += 1) {798        if (kayan_matches(kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32))*.signature, q*.all, q*.none)) {799            _ = vec<u32>push(q*.tables, cast(ti, u32));800        }801    }802    q*.checked = w*.tables*.length;803}804 805// The query's i-th table.806kayan_query_table: proc(w: *const kayan_world, q: *const kayan_query, i: u64) -> *kayan_table in level = {807    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<u32>at(q*.tables, i)*);808}809 810// How many entities the query matches: the rows of its tables.811kayan_query_count: proc(w: *const kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> u64 = {812    kayan_query_update(w, q);813    n: u64 = 0;814    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q*.tables*.length; i += 1) {815        n += kayan_query_table(w, q, i)*.count;816    }817    return n;818}819 820kayan_print_query: proc(w: *const kayan_world, name: ^const char, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {821    kayan_query_update(w, q);822    printfmt("{}: all ", name);823    kayan_print_signature(w, q*.all);824    printfmt(", none ");825    kayan_print_signature(w, q*.none);826    printfmt("; tables: {}, entities: {}\n", q*.tables*.length, kayan_query_count(w, q));827    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q*.tables*.length; i += 1) {828        kayan_print_table(w, vec<u32>at(q*.tables, i)*);829    }830}831 832// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------833// Systems834// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------835 836// What a system gets for each table it runs on: the world, the table, and the837// frame's time step. One struct rather than three parameters, so that adding838// to it later changes no system's signature. Both pointers name their region,839// so the struct can be made anywhere level is open.840kayan_iter: struct = {841    world: *kayan_world in level;842    table: *kayan_table in level;843    dt: f32;844}845 846kayan_system_proc: alias = *proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void;847 848// A system is code: a name, and the proc run on each table its query matches.849// A C string and a proc pointer are both pointers without a region, so a850// struct holding them is a carrier: safe code reaches it only through a851// pointer into a region, made by a trusted proc. Neither changes after it is852// made, so nothing is lost.853kayan_system: struct = {854    name: ^const char;855    run: kayan_system_proc;856}857 858kayan_system_make: proc(r: region level, name: ^const char, run: kayan_system_proc) -> *kayan_system in level = {859    unsafe {860        s: *kayan_system in level = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(r, sizeof(kayan_system), alignof(kayan_system)), *kayan_system in level);861        s*.name = name;862        s*.run = run;863        return s;864    }865}866 867// A system in the schedule: which system, the query that finds its tables,868// and what it has run over so far. `tables` and `rows` count the calls.869kayan_scheduled: struct = {870    system: *kayan_system in level;871    query: kayan_query;872    tables: u64;873    rows: u64;874}875 876// The schedule is a list of these, in the order the frame runs them. Each877// entry is its own allocation so a pointer to one is a pointer into level,878// which the checker never counts as stale.879kayan_schedule_add: proc(r: region level, systems: *vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>, name: ^const char,880                         all: u64, none: u64, run: kayan_system_proc) -> void = {881    _ = vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>push(systems, new<kayan_scheduled>(r, {882        .system = kayan_system_make(r, name, run),883        .query = kayan_query_init(r, all, none),884    }));885}886 887kayan_scheduled_at: proc(systems: *const vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>, s: u64) -> *kayan_scheduled in level = {888    return vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>at_const(systems, s)*;889}890 891// One frame: every system in order, each over every table it matches that has892// rows. s < systems*.length; s += 1) {895        sys: *kayan_scheduled in level = kayan_scheduled_at(systems, s);896        kayan_query_update(w, sys*.query&);897        for (i: u64 = 0; i < sys*.query.tables*.length; i += 1) {898            it: kayan_iter = { .world = w, .table = kayan_query_table(w, sys*.query&, i), .dt = dt };899            if (it.table*.count > 0) {900                sys*.tables += 1;901                sys*.rows += it.table*.count;902                sys*.system*.run(it&);903            }904        }905    }906}907 908kayan_print_schedule: proc(w: *const kayan_world, systems: *const vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>) -> void = {909    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems*.length; s += 1) {910        sys: *kayan_scheduled in level = kayan_scheduled_at(systems, s);911        kayan_print_query(w, sys*.system*.name, sys*.query&);912    }913}914 915// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------916// The program917// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------918 919// Kernels: plain loops over plain slices, with components for elements.920// noalias on what each one writes, as in lessons 1 to 7.921integrate: proc[unsafe](ps: noalias []position, vs: []const velocity, dt: f32) -> void = {922    for (i: u64 = 0; i < ps.length; i += 1) {923        ps[i].at.x += vs[i].per_second.x * dt;924        ps[i].at.y += vs[i].per_second.y * dt;925    }926}927 928burn: proc[unsafe](hs: noalias []health, fires: []const burning, dt: f32) -> void = {929    for (i: u64 = 0; i < hs.length; i += 1) {930        hs[i].points -= fires[i].per_second * dt;931    }932}933 934age: proc[unsafe](ls: noalias []lifetime, dt: f32) -> void = {935    for (i: u64 = 0; i < ls.length; i += 1) {936        ls[i].seconds -= dt;937    }938}939 940// Systems: the table's columns, handed to a kernel.941move_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {942    unsafe { integrate(kayan_slice<position>(it*.table), kayan_slice<velocity>(it*.table), it*.dt); }943}944 945burn_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {946    unsafe { burn(kayan_slice<health>(it*.table), kayan_slice<burning>(it*.table), it*.dt); }947}948 949age_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {950    unsafe { age(kayan_slice<lifetime>(it*.table), it*.dt); }951}952 953spawn_turret: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32) -> kayan_entity = {954    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<turret>());955    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = y } });956    _ = kayan_set<turret>(w, e, { .cooldown = 0.5, .timer = 0.0 });957    return e;958}959 960spawn_drone: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32) -> kayan_entity = {961    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>() | kayan_mask_of<health>());962    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = y } });963    _ = kayan_set<velocity>(w, e, { .per_second = { .x = -1.0, .y = 0.0 } });964    _ = kayan_set<health>(w, e, { .points = 100.0, .max = 100.0 });965    return e;966}967 968spawn_bullet: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32, seconds: f32) -> kayan_entity = {969    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>()970        | kayan_mask_of<damage>() | kayan_mask_of<lifetime>());971    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = y } });972    _ = kayan_set<velocity>(w, e, { .per_second = { .x = 8.0, .y = 0.0 } });973    _ = kayan_set<damage>(w, e, { .amount = 25.0 });974    _ = kayan_set<lifetime>(w, e, { .seconds = seconds });975    return e;976}977 978// Every entity, with the components this program cares about. Each value is979// copied out of its pointer before the next lookup: a lookup takes the world,980// and a pointer into it does not survive that in the checker's eyes.981print_state: proc(w: *const kayan_world) -> void = {982    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w*.tables*.length, u32); ti += 1) {983        t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, ti);984        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t*.count; row += 1) {985            es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(t);986            e: kayan_entity = es[row];987            p: option<*position> = kayan_get<position>(w, e);988            if (!p) {989                continue;990            }991            at: vec2 = p*.at;992            printfmt("    {}:{} at ({:5.2}, {:5.2})", e.index, e.generation, cast(at.x, f64), cast(at.y, f64));993            h: cast(l*.seconds, f64));1003            }1004            printfmt("\n");1005        }1006    }1007}1008 1009main: proc() -> i32 = {1010    level: region = {1011        w: *kayan_world in level = kayan_id_of<turret>(), turret<>&);1018        kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<burning>(), burning<>&);1019 1020        _ = spawn_turret(w, 0.0, 0.0);1021        _ = spawn_drone(w, 20.0, 4.0);1022        hot: kayan_entity = spawn_drone(w, 24.0, 0.0);1023        _ = spawn_drone(w, 28.0, -4.0);1024        _ = kayan_add<burning>(w, hot, { .per_second = 8.0 });1025        _ = spawn_bullet(w, 1.0, 0.0, 0.5);1026        _ = spawn_bullet(w, 1.0, 4.0, 1.0);1027        _ = spawn_bullet(w, 1.0, -4.0, 1.5);1028 1029        // The schedule. The order is the data flow: a system that reads what1030        // another writes runs after it.1031        systems: *vec<*kayan_scheduled in level> in level = vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>make(level, 3);1032        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "burn", kayan_mask_of<health>() | kayan_mask_of<burning>(), 0, burn_system);1033        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "age", kayan_mask_of<lifetime>(), 0, age_system);1034        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "move", kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>(), 0, move_system);1035        printfmt("the schedule, run in this order every frame:\n");1036        kayan_print_schedule(w, systems);1037        printfmt("\nat the start:\n");1038        print_state(w);1039 1040        dt: f32 = 0.25;1041        for (frame: u32 = 1; Build an ECS · part 3, systems · 3.3

Commands

ecs/src/3.systems/3.3.commands/commands.rin

In the dojo: 5. a command buffer, 7. an arena, each on its own, to watch and to practise.

3.2's systems change values, never structure, so bullets whose time ran out stay in the world. The obvious fix is to despawn them from inside the system. It's wrong, and seeing exactly why is most of this chapter.

Step 1: the bug

expire_now_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {
    t: *kayan_table in level = it*.table;
    for (row: u64 = 0; row < t*.count; row += 1) {
        ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(t);
        es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(t);
        if (ls[row].seconds <= 0.0) {
            _ = kayan_despawn(it*.world, es[row]);
        }
    }
}

Four bullets, three of them out of time:

1. an expire system that despawns as it goes
    lifetimes:  0:1 0.00  1:1 1.00  2:1 0.00  3:1 0.00
after one frame:
    lifetimes:  3:1 0.00  1:1 1.00
kayan_verify: 0 problems. The world is fine; the loop missed one.

Row by row:

row 0: 0:1 is out of time. Despawn: the last row, 3:1, moves into row 0.
row 1: 1:1 has time left.
row 2: 2:1 is out of time. Despawn: it's the last row, so nothing moves.
row 3: the table has 2 rows now. Stop.

3:1 moved into row 0, which the loop had already passed, so it was never looked at. The world is perfectly consistent (kayan_verify agrees). The loop is what's wrong: a despawn swap-removes from the table the loop is walking.

The checker lets this through, and it isn't wrong to. The slices are taken again each time round, every read is in bounds, and nothing touches bad memory. A missed row is a logic bug, and that's the kind of bug a loop over indices leaves you with. No memory checker is coming to help here. The fix has to be a design.

Walking backwards fixes this case (lesson 2 does it), because the row that moves in has already been looked at. But it doesn't fix the general problem:

  • Adding or removing a component moves the entity to another table. If the query matches that table too and visits it later, the entity is processed twice.
  • That move adds a row, and if the destination table is full, its columns grow and move. A slice into that table is then looking at the old block, which the region still owns, so nothing crashes and every write through it is lost. This is 2.5's bug, from inside a loop. A slice is a borrow, and the checker ends a borrow when it can see the world changing beneath it. Inside a system it can't always: the table and the world both arrive through it, and it has no way to connect them. So the region keeps this safe, and something else has to keep it right.
  • One system's despawn can land in a table another system is halfway through, if a system despawns entities it found through a second query.

Step 2: record now, apply later

So a system doesn't change structure. It records a command saying what should change, and the world applies every command after the frame's last system:

during the frame   values change; tables, rows and pointers do not
after the frame    spawns, despawns, adds and removes, in order
kayan_command_kind: enum = {
    spawn,
    despawn,
    add,
    remove,
}

kayan_command: struct = {
    kind: kayan_command_kind;
    entity: kayan_entity;
    spawn: u32;
    id: u32;
    signature: u64;
    value: []u8 in frame;
}

A command names the entity, and for an add or remove the component id. An add carries its value as bytes. The bytes, and the list of commands, are only needed until the end of the frame, so they get memory that ends with the frame. That's a second region:

level: region;
frame: region in level;

in level says frame opens and ends inside level. So memory in frame may point into level, since level will still be there. The other way round is refused, and that's what makes this shape safe. Try to keep a command in the world, and it doesn't compile:

type error: this points into region 'frame', which may end before the memory in region 'level' that holds it

So no command can outlive its frame, by construction, and no one has to remember to check. The buffer is the commands and the arena their values are copied into:

kayan_commands: struct = {
    heap: *kayan_heap in frame;
    list: *vec<kayan_command> in frame;
}

kayan_commands_make: proc(r: region frame) -> *kayan_commands in frame = {
    return new<kayan_commands>(r, { .heap = kayan_heap_make(r), .list = vec<kayan_command>make(r, 16) });
}

and a frame opens the region, makes the buffer, runs, and ends:

run_frame: proc(w: *kayan_world in level, systems: *const vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>, dt: f32) -> void = {
    frame: region = {
        kayan_progress(w, systems, dt, kayan_commands_make(frame));
    }
}

There's no line that drops the commands. The end of that block is it, whatever they were. A loop variable can't be called frame any more, either, now that it names a region, so these chapters count frame_no.

Systems reach the buffer through their iterator, which gains two fields:

kayan_iter: struct = {
    world: *kayan_world in level;
    table: *kayan_table in level;
    dt: f32;
    commands: *kayan_commands in frame;
    ctx: option<*kayan_query in level>;
}

Step 3: recording

The typed procs a system calls copy the value into the frame's arena and append a command:

kayan_defer_value: proc<T>(h: *kayan_heap in frame, value: T) -> []u8 in frame = {
    unsafe {
        data: ^u8 = cast(memops_arena_push(h*.arena[0]&, sizeof(T), alignof(T)), ^u8);
        memcpy(data, value&, sizeof(T));
        return cast(data[0..sizeof(T)], []u8 in frame);
    }
}

That's the command buffer's one trusted proc, because a value's bytes are a cast. Its signature says what matters: the bytes are in frame, so they get the same protection as the command that holds them.

kayan_defer_add: proc<T>(cmds: *kayan_commands, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> void = {
    _ = kayan_defer(cmds, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.add, .entity = e, .id = kayan_id_of<T>(),
        .value = kayan_defer_value<T>(cmds*.heap, value) });
}

The fixed expire system is the broken one with one word changed:

expire_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {
    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(it*.table);
    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it*.table);
    for (row: u64 = 0; row < es.length; row += 1) {
        if (ls[row].seconds <= 0.0) {
            kayan_defer_despawn(it*.commands, es[row]);
        }
    }
}

Now the table doesn't change while the loop runs, so the loop can take the entities as a slice up front, like any other column.

Step 4: applying, by id

Commands hold bytes and ids, not types. So applying an add needs 2.6's add by id:

kayan_add_id: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32, value: []const u8) -> kayan_status = {
    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {
        return kayan_status.dead;
    }
    from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.table;
    if (!kayan_table_has(kayan_table_at(w, from), id)) {
        kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_with(w, from, id));
    }
    bytes: []u8 = kayan_get_bytes(w, e, id);
    if (value.length != bytes.length) {
        printfmt("kayan: a {}-byte value for a component of {} bytes\n", value.length, bytes.length);
        exit(1);
    }
    for (i: u64 = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1) {
        bytes[i] = value[i];
    }
    return kayan_status.ok;
}

It's the same move-then-write as before, with the write a checked loop over the value's bytes. Once that exists, the typed kayan_remove<T> from 2.6 shrinks to a one-line wrapper. That's the pattern from the start of the course: byte fiddling written once, a type-safe generic layer on top.

kayan_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {
    return kayan_remove_id(w, e, kayan_id_of<T>());
}

kayan_add<T> keeps its 2.6 body instead of calling this one. To go through kayan_add_id it would have to turn its T into bytes, and that's a cast, which would make it another trusted proc. It moves the entity and calls kayan_set<T> instead, and stays checked. The boundary between typed and untyped code is somewhere you want as few crossings as possible.

kayan_flush walks the list in order and applies each command. It's called at the end of kayan_progress:

    kayan_flush(w, cmds);
}

Step 5: commands that arrive too late

By the time a command is applied, its entity may be gone. The usual case is two systems both asking to despawn the same thing. Applying in order handles that for free: the first despawn works, and the second finds a dead handle. Part 1's generations make that check one comparison:

        if (status == kayan_status.ok) {
            w*.applied += 1;
        } else {
            w*.skipped += 1;
        }

Step 6: spawning from a system

A turret firing is a spawn in the middle of a frame. The new entity doesn't exist until the commands are applied, so there's no handle to give its components to. kayan_defer_spawn returns a pending spawn instead: the spawn command's place in the list. Components are given to that:

            shot: kayan_pending = kayan_defer_spawn(it*.commands, bullet_signature());
            kayan_pending_set<position>(it*.commands, shot, ps[row]);
            kayan_pending_set<velocity>(it*.commands, shot, { .per_second = { .x = 8.0, .y = 0.0 } });
            kayan_pending_set<damage>(it*.commands, shot, { .amount = 25.0 });
            kayan_pending_set<lifetime>(it*.commands, shot, { .seconds = 2.0 });

When the flush reaches the spawn, it makes the entity and writes the handle into the command. The adds after it look the handle up there. The bullet is spawned with its full signature, so the adds land in the table it's already in: no moves. And it doesn't move until the next frame, because no system ran over it this one.

The flush allocates in level, deep inside a frame, with no level in sight. This is why 3.1 had the world remember its region.

Step 7: a system with two queries

A bullet that reaches a target damages it. The hit system walks the bullets (its own query) and, for each, the targets (a second query). It reaches the second query through a new field, ctx, which kayan passes through untouched:

    targets: option<*kayan_query in level> = it*.ctx;
    if (!targets) {
        return;
    }

ctx is a typed pointer rather than a *void, because the checker has to know what it points at. A system with no second query gets null, so the ones that use it test it first.

The damage is a value, so it's written now. The bullet's despawn is structure, so it's recorded. Walking a second query in the middle of a frame is safe because of commands: no table is made and no column moves until the frame is over. The slices in this system stay true for the whole frame, and that's the guarantee no checker gave us: the design did.

In frame 4, bullet 4:1 is close enough to both targets. Both lose 25, and both hits record a despawn. The first applies; the second finds 4:1 already dead and is skipped. In frame 5 the next bullet gets number 4 back with generation 2: Part 1, working.

17 commands, for three bullets and two despawns: each spawn is five, the spawn and its four components.

Try

  1. In expire_now_system, take ls and es once, before the loop, and loop to ls.length instead of t*.count. It still compiles, and now all three get despawned. Work out why. (Hint: what's in the rows past the end of the table?) Is that loop correct?
  2. Write a system that adds burning directly (not deferred) to every target it walks. Count how many times it visits each entity.
  3. Flush after each system instead of after the frame. You'll have to empty the list after each flush, with vec<kayan_command>clear(cmds*.list), since it's no longer the region's end that lets the commands go. What does that change about what later systems see? (flecs calls these sync points.)
  4. Add a field kept: option<*kayan_commands in frame>; to kayan_world, and compile. Which rule did you just run into, and what bug is it saving you from?

The old storage is147// left in the region: a slice taken before the grow still points at valid148// memory, and stale values.149kayan_column_grow: proc(h: *kayan_heap, c: *kayan_column, count: u64, capacity: u64) -> void = {150    unsafe {151        raw: ^u8 = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(h*.arena[0]&, c*.size * capacity, c*.align), ^u8);152        bytes: []u8 in level = cast(raw[0..c*.size * capacity], []u8 in level);153        // Slicing checks both ends: a count past either block stops the program.154        kept: u64 = c*.size * count;155        slice<u8>copy(bytes[0..kept], c*.data[0..kept]);156        c*.data = bytes;157    }158}159 160// One row's bytes, bounds-checked like any slice.161kayan_column_bytes: proc(c: *kayan_column, row: u64) -> []u8 in level = {162    return c*.data[row * c*.size..(row + 1) * c*.size];163}164 165// The typed view: the column's first `count` rows as `[]T`. After the column grows it is the172// old block, still readable, no longer the column: take the view again.173kayan_column_slice: proc<T>(c: *const kayan_column, count: u64) -> []T in level = {174    if (c*.size != sizeof(T)) {175        printfmt("kayan: a column of {}-byte rows read as a {}-byte type\n", c*.size, sizeof(T));176        exit(1);177    }178    if (!reflect_is_plain(T<>&)) {179        printfmt("kayan: a column holds plain data, and this {}-byte type is not\n", sizeof(T));180        exit(1);181    }182    if (count > c*.data.length / sizeof(T)) {183        printfmt("kayan: a view of {} rows on a column with room for {}\n", count, c*.data.length / sizeof(T));184        exit(1);185    }186    unsafe {187        if (cast(c*.data.data, usize) % alignof(T) != 0) {188            printfmt("kayan: a column's bytes are not aligned to {}\n", alignof(T));189            exit(1);190        }191        raw: ^T = cast(c*.data.data, ^T);192        return cast(raw[0..count], []T in level);193    }194}195 196// Copying and zeroing a row are loops over the row's bytes: checked code.197kayan_column_copy_row: proc(c: *kayan_column, to: u64, from: u64) -> void = {198    dst: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(c, to);199    src: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(c, from);200    for (i: u64 = 0; i < dst.length; i += 1) {201        dst[i] = src[i];202    }203}204 205kayan_column_zero_row: proc(c: *kayan_column, row: u64) -> void = {206    bytes: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(c, row);207    for (i: u64 = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1) {208        bytes[i] = 0;209    }210}211 212// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------213// The table214// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------215 216// `columns[id]` is a column when the signature has bit `id`, and null217// otherwise. Count and capacity are the table's, shared by its columns, so218// they can never disagree; `entities` grows on its own and always has `count`219// rows.220//221// The edges: `add_edges[id]` is the table this one's entities move to when222// they gain component `id`, and `remove_edges[id]` when they lose it. Each is223// the table's index plus one, so 0, which a new table starts with, means "not224// known yet".225kayan_table: struct = {226    signature: u64;227    count: u64;228    capacity: u64;229    entities: *vec<kayan_entity> in level;230    columns: [64]option<*kayan_column in level>;231    add_edges: [64]u32;232    remove_edges: [64]u32;233}234 235// A zeroed table in the region, with an empty entities vec: the world fills236// in the signature and the columns.237kayan_table_new: proc(h: *kayan_heap in level) -> *kayan_table in level = {238    unsafe {239        t: *kayan_table in level = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(h*.arena[0]&, sizeof(kayan_table), alignof(kayan_table)), *kayan_table in level);240        v: *vec<kayan_entity> in level = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(h*.arena[0]&, sizeof(vec<kayan_entity>), alignof(vec<kayan_entity>)), *vec<kayan_entity> in level);241        v*.arena = h*.arena;242        t*.entities = v;243        return t;244    }245}246 247// The world: the registry, the slots and free list, and every table, with a248// map from signature to table index so finding one is a lookup, not a search.249// Tables are referred to by index, so a table can be named in a slot; each250// table is its own allocation, so a pointer to one stays good when the next251// is made.252kayan_world: struct = {253    heap: *kayan_heap in level;254    infos: [64]option<*const reflect in permanent>;255    component_count: u32;256    tables: *vec<*kayan_table in level> in level;257    by_signature: *hashmap<u64, u32> in level;258    slots: *vec<kayan_slot> in level;259    free: *vec<u32> in level;260    live: u64;261    // What the flushes did, and whether to print each command as it is applied.262    applied: u64;263    skipped: u64;264    trace: b32;265}266 267kayan_bit: proc(id: u32) -> u64 = {268    return 1'u64 shl cast(id, u64);269}270 271kayan_id_of: proc<T>() -> u32 = {272    return cast(component_of<T>(), u32);273}274 275kayan_mask_of: proc<T>() -> u64 = {276    return kayan_bit(kayan_id_of<T>());277}278 279// The reflect records live for the whole program, so `permanent` is their280// region and the world may keep them.281kayan_register: proc(w: *kayan_world, id: u32, info: *const reflect in permanent) -> void = {282    if (id >= 64) {283        printfmt("kayan: component id {} is past the 64 a signature can hold\n", id);284        exit(1);285    }286    w*.infos[id] = info;287    if (id + 1 > w*.component_count) {288        w*.component_count = id + 1;289    }290}291 292// A registered component's record. The checker needs the null test; the293// return after exit is never reached.294kayan_info: proc(w: *const kayan_world, id: u32) -> *const reflect in permanent = {295    info: option<*const reflect in permanent> = w*.infos[id];296    if (info) {297        return info;298    }299    printfmt("kayan: component {} was never registered\n", id);300    exit(1);301    return kayan_entity<>&;302}303 304kayan_table_has: proc(t: *const kayan_table, id: u32) -> b32 = {305    return (t*.signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0;306}307 308// A table for a signature: one empty column per component in it, sized from309// the registry. Every component in the signature must be registered.310kayan_table_make: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> *kayan_table in level = {311    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_new(w*.heap);312    t*.signature = signature;313    for (id: u32 = 0; id < 64; id += 1) {314        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {315            if (id >= w*.component_count) {316                printfmt("kayan: signature {} uses component {}, which was never registered\n", signature, id);317                exit(1);318            }319            t*.columns[id] = kayan_column_make(w*.heap, kayan_info(w, id));320        }321    }322    return t;323}324 325// Double the room in every column at once.326kayan_table_grow: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table) -> void = {327    capacity: u64 = t*.capacity == 0 ? 4 : t*.capacity * 2;328    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {329        c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];330        if (c) {331            kayan_column_grow(w*.heap, c, t*.count, capacity);332        }333    }334    t*.capacity = capacity;335}336 337// A new row at the end, owned by `e`, with every component zeroed.338kayan_table_add_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {339    if (t*.count == t*.capacity) {340        kayan_table_grow(w, t);341    }342    row: u64 = t*.count;343    t*.count += 1;344    _ = vec<kayan_entity>push(t*.entities, e);345    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {346        c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];347        if (c) {348            kayan_column_zero_row(c, row);349        }350    }351    return row;352}353 354// Who owns each of the table's rows. It only reads, and the checker sees that,355// so a system holds this and two or three columns of one table at once.356kayan_entities: proc(t: *const kayan_table) -> []kayan_entity in level = {357    return vec<kayan_entity>items(t*.entities);358}359 360// 1.4's swap-remove, for every column: the last row is copied over `row`, and361// the slot of the entity that owned the last row is told where it went.362kayan_table_remove_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, row: u64) -> void = {363    last: u64 = t*.count - 1;364    if (row != last) {365        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {366            c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];367            if (c) {368                kayan_column_copy_row(c, row, last);369            }370        }371        moved: kayan_entity = vec<kayan_entity>at(t*.entities, last)*;372        vec<kayan_entity>at(t*.entities, row)* = moved;373        vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(moved.index, u64))*.row = cast(row, u32);374    }375    _ = vec<kayan_entity>pop(t*.entities);376    t*.count = last;377}378 379// The typed view of one of the table's columns: T's rows, all of them in use.380// Asking for a component the table does not have is a bug, so it stops. The381// slice is good memory for as long as the region, but when the table grows it is382// the old block, no longer the column: take it again, and 3.3 makes that a rule.383kayan_slice: proc<T>(t: *const kayan_table) -> []T in level = {384    id: u32 = kayan_id_of<T>();385    c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];386    if (!c) {387        printfmt("kayan: the table has no column for component {}\n", id);388        exit(1);389    }390    return kayan_column_slice<T>(c, t*.count);391}392 393kayan_table_at: proc(w: *const kayan_world, index: u32) -> *kayan_table in level = {394    return vec<*kayan_table in level>at(w*.tables, cast(index, u64))*;395}396 397// The table for a signature: found if it exists, made if it does not. This is398// where archetypes come from.399kayan_table_for: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> u32 = {400    found: option<*u32> = hashmap<u64, u32>get(w*.by_signature, signature);401    if (found) {402        return found*;403    }404    index: u32 = cast(w*.tables*.length, u32);405    _ = vec<*kayan_table in level>push(w*.tables, kayan_table_make(w, signature));406    _ = hashmap<u64, u32>set(w*.by_signature, signature, index);407    return index;408}409 410// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------411// The world412// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------413 414kayan_world_make: proc(r: region level) -> *kayan_world in level = {415    return new<kayan_world>(r, {416        .heap = kayan_heap_make(r),417        .tables = vec<*kayan_table in level>make(r, 8),418        .by_signature = hashmap<u64, u32>make(r),419        .slots = vec<kayan_slot>make(r, 64),420        .free = vec<u32>make(r, 16),421    });422}423 424kayan_alive: proc(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {425    if (cast(e.index, u64) >= w*.slots*.length) {426        return false;427    }428    return vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.generation == e.generation;429}430 431// A new entity with the components in `signature`, all zeroed, in the table432// for that signature.433kayan_spawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> kayan_entity = {434    e: kayan_entity = {};435    if (w*.free*.length > 0) {436        e.index = vec<u32>pop(w*.free);437    } else {438        e.index = cast(w*.slots*.length, u32);439        _ = vec<kayan_slot>push(w*.slots, { .generation = 1 });440    }441    e.generation = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.generation;442    table_index: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, signature);443    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, table_index);444    row: u64 = kayan_table_add_row(w, t, e);445    // The slot is taken after the calls that change the world: a pointer into446    // `slots` from before them may be stale, and the checker says so.447    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));448    slot*.table = table_index;449    slot*.row = cast(row, u32);450    w*.live += 1;451    return e;452}453 454kayan_despawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {455    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {456        return kayan_status.dead;457    }458    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));459    table: u32 = slot*.table;460    row: u32 = slot*.row;461    kayan_table_remove_row(w, kayan_table_at(w, table), cast(row, u64));462    slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));463    slot*.generation += 1;464    _ = vec<u32>push(w*.free, e.index);465    w*.live -= 1;466    return kayan_status.ok;467}468 469// The components a live entity has: its table's signature. 0 for a dead one.470kayan_signature: proc(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {471    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {472        return 0;473    }474    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots,
