---------------------------------------------------------------------------480 481// The table an entity of table `from` moves to when it gains component `id`.482// The first time, it is found by signature, which can make the table; the483// answer is written on both tables, as from's add edge and the destination's484// remove edge, so neither direction is looked up again.485kayan_table_with: proc(w: *kayan_world, from: u32, id: u32) -> u32 = {486    edge: u32 = kayan_table_at(w, from)*.add_edges[id];487    if (edge != 0) {488        return edge - 1;489    }490    to: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, kayan_table_at(w, from)*.signature | kayan_bit(id));491    kayan_table_at(w, from)*.add_edges[id] = to + 1;492    kayan_table_at(w, to)*.remove_edges[id] = from + 1;493    return to;494}495 496// The same for losing component `id`.497kayan_table_without: proc(w: *kayan_world, from: u32, id: u32) -> u32 = {498    edge: u32 = kayan_table_at(w, from)*.remove_edges[id];499    if (edge != 0) {500        return edge - 1;501    }502    to: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, kayan_table_at(w, from)*.signature & ~kayan_bit(id));503    kayan_table_at(w, from)*.remove_edges[id] = to + 1;504    kayan_table_at(w, to)*.add_edges[id] = from + 1;505    return to;506}507 508// Move a live entity to table `to_index`. Components both tables have are509// copied, byte for byte; components only the new table has start zeroed;510// components only the old table has are dropped with its old row.511kayan_move: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, to_index: u32) -> void = {512    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));513    from_index: u32 = slot*.table;514    if (from_index == to_index) {515        return;516    }517    from_row: u64 = cast(slot*.row, u64);518    from: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, from_index);519    to: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, to_index);520    to_row: u64 = kayan_table_add_row(w, to, e);521    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {522        fc: option<*kayan_column in level> = from*.columns[id];523        tc: option<*kayan_column in level> = to*.columns[id];524        if (fc && tc) {525            dst: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(tc, to_row);526            src: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(fc, from_row);527            for (i: u64 = 0; i < dst.length; i += 1) {528                dst[i] = src[i];529            }530        }531    }532    kayan_table_remove_row(w, from, from_row);533    slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));534    slot*.table = to_index;535    slot*.row = cast(to_row, u32);536}537 538// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------539// The byte layer, for tools and for commands540// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------541 542// Give e component `id`, with `value` for its bytes: 2.6's add, by id instead543// of by type, because a command holds its value as bytes. The copy is a loop544// over two slices the checker has sized.545kayan_add_id: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32, value: []const u8) -> kayan_status = {546    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {547        return kayan_status.dead;548    }549    from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.table;550    if (!kayan_table_has(kayan_table_at(w, from), id)) {551        kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_with(w, from, id));552    }553    bytes: []u8 = kayan_get_bytes(w, e, id);554    if (value.length != bytes.length) {555        printfmt("kayan: a {}-byte value for a component of {} bytes\n", value.length, bytes.length);556        exit(1);557    }558    for (i: u64 = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1) {559        bytes[i] = value[i];560    }561    return kayan_status.ok;562}563 564kayan_remove_id: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32) -> kayan_status = {565    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {566        return kayan_status.dead;567    }568    from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.table;569    if (!kayan_table_has(kayan_table_at(w, from), id)) {570        return kayan_status.missing;571    }572    kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_without(w, from, id));573    return kayan_status.ok;574}575 576// e's component `id` as its bytes: an empty slice if e is dead or has no such577// component. The typed layer is for game code, which knows its types; this is578// for tools that work from reflect records instead.579kayan_get_bytes: proc(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32) -> []u8 in level = {580    none: []u8 in level = {};581    if (!kayan_alive(w, e) || id >= w*.component_count) {582        return none;583    }584    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));585    table: u32 = slot*.table;586    row: u32 = slot*.row;587    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, table);588    c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];589    if (!c) {590        return none;591    }592    return kayan_column_bytes(c, cast(row, u64));593}594 595// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------596// The typed layer597// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------598 599// e's T, or null if e is dead or has no T. Handle, slot, table, row, typed600// view: the same path as 1.4's get_position, for any component. `option<*T>` says the601// null is possible, so the caller tests before it reads. The pointer is good602// until the next structural change, so use it now and keep the handle.603kayan_get: proc<T>(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> option<*T in level> = {604    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {605        return null;606    }607    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));608    table: u32 = slot*.table;609    row: u32 = slot*.row;610    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, table);611    if (!kayan_table_has(t, kayan_id_of<T>())) {612        return null;613    }614    rows: []T in level = kayan_slice<T>(t);615    return rows[cast(row, u64)]&;616}617 618kayan_has: proc<T>(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {619    return (kayan_signature(w, e) & kayan_mask_of<T>()) != 0;620}621 622// Write e's T. It must already have one: giving an entity a component it does623// not have changes its table, which is 2.6.624kayan_set: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {625    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {626        return kayan_status.dead;627    }628    p: option<*T> = kayan_get<T>(w, e);629    if (!p) {630        return kayan_status.missing;631    }632    p* = value;633    return kayan_status.ok;634}635 636// Give e a T. If it already has one, this is kayan_set; if not, it moves to637// the table with T and then sets it.638kayan_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {639    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {640        return kayan_status.dead;641    }642    if (!kayan_has<T>(w, e)) {643        from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.table;644        kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_with(w, from, kayan_id_of<T>()));645    }646    return kayan_set<T>(w, e, value);647}648 649// Take e's T away: the byte proc, with the type turned into an id.650kayan_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {651    return kayan_remove_id(w, e, kayan_id_of<T>());652}653 654// The invariant, over every table: each row belongs to a live entity whose655// slot points back at that table and row, and the rows of all tables add up to656// the live count.657kayan_verify: proc(w: *const kayan_world) -> u64 = {658    problems: u64 = 0;659    rows: u64 = 0;660    for (ti: u64 = 0; ti < w*.tables*.length; ti += 1) {661        t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32));662        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t*.count; row += 1) {663            // Taken row by row: kayan_alive takes the world, and the checker664            // does not know that it leaves the rows where they are.665            es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(t);666            e: kayan_entity = es[row];667            if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {668                printfmt("kayan_verify: table {} row {} holds dead entity {}:{}\n", ti, row, e.index, e.generation);669                problems += 1;670                continue;671            }672            slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));673            if (cast(slot*.table, u64) != ti || cast(slot*.row, u64) != row) {674                printfmt("kayan_verify: {}:{} is in table {} row {}, its slot says table {} row {}\n",675                    e.index, e.generation, ti, row, slot*.table, slot*.row);676                problems += 1;677            }678        }679        rows += t*.count;680    }681    if (rows != w*.live) {682        printfmt("kayan_verify: {} rows in tables, {} live entities\n", rows, w*.live);683        problems += 1;684    }685    return problems;686}687 688kayan_print_signature: proc(w: *const kayan_world, signature: u64) -> void = {689    printfmt("{");690    first: b32 = true;691    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {692        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {693            if (!first) {694                printfmt(" ");695            }696            printfmt("{}", kayan_info(w, id)*.name);697            first = false;698        }699    }700    printfmt("}");701}702 703kayan_print_table: proc(w: *const kayan_world, ti: u32) -> void = {704    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, ti);705    printfmt("    table {} ", ti);706    kayan_print_signature(w, t*.signature);707    printfmt(":");708    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(t);709    for (row: u64 = 0; row < es.length; row += 1) {710        e: kayan_entity = es[row];711        printfmt(" {}:{}", e.index, e.generation);712    }713    printfmt("\n");714}715 716kayan_print_tables: proc(w: *const kayan_world) -> void = {717    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w*.tables*.length, u32); ti += 1) {718        kayan_print_table(w, ti);719    }720}721 722// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------723// The inspector: reflect records, no component types724// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------725 726kayan_indent: proc(depth: u32) -> void = {727    for (i: u32 = 0; i < depth; i += 1) {728        printfmt("    ");729    }730}731 732// One value of a builtin type, read from its bytes by its type's name. The733// bytes may sit at any address, so the read is a copy into a local: this is the734// inspector's one unsafe block.735kayan_print_builtin: proc(type_name: ^const char, at: []const u8) -> void = {736    if (at.length < 4) {737        printfmt("<{} bytes>", at.length);738        return;739    }740    unsafe {741        if (reflect_cstr_equal(type_name, "f32")) {742            f: f32 = 0.0;743            memcpy(f&, at.data, 4);744            printfmt("{:.2}", cast(f, f64));745        } else if (reflect_cstr_equal(type_name, "u32")) {746            u: u32 = 0;747            memcpy(u&, at.data, 4);748            printfmt("{}", u);749        } else if (reflect_cstr_equal(type_name, "i32")) {750            i: i32 = 0;751            memcpy(i&, at.data, 4);752            printfmt("{}", i);753        } else {754            printfmt("<{}>", type_name);755        }756    }757}758 759// Every field of a struct whose bytes are `base`, nested structs indented760// under their field. A field's bytes are cut from `base` by its offset and761// size, both from the reflect record.762kayan_print_fields: proc(type: *const reflect, base: []const u8, depth: u32) -> void = {763    for (i: u64 = 0; i < type*.count; i += 1) {764        f: option<*const reflect_field> = reflect_field_at(type, i);765        if (!f) {766            continue;767        }768        if (reflect_field_has_attr(f, "hidden")) {769            continue;770        }771        at: []const u8 = base[f*.offset..f*.offset + f*.size];772        kayan_indent(depth);773        printfmt("{}:", f*.name);774        info: option<*const reflect> = reflect_field_info(f);775        if (info && info*.kind == reflect_kind_struct) {776            printfmt("\n");777            kayan_print_fields(info, at, depth + 1);778        } else {779            printfmt(" ");780            kayan_print_builtin(f*.type, at);781            printfmt("\n");782        }783    }784}785 786kayan_inspect: proc(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {787    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {788        printfmt("{}:{} (dead)\n", e.index, e.generation);789        return;790    }791    printfmt("{}:{} ", e.index, e.generation);792    signature: u64 = kayan_signature(w, e);793    kayan_print_signature(w, signature);794    printfmt("\n");795    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {796        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {797            info: *const reflect in permanent = kayan_info(w, id);798            printfmt("    {}\n", info*.name);799            bytes: []u8 = kayan_get_bytes(w, e, id);800            kayan_print_fields(info, bytes, 2);801        }802    }803}804 805// Every table: rows in use out of room, and per column its row size and its806// bytes in use out of bytes allocated. The memory a table holds and does not807// use is the cost of doubling on growth.808kayan_print_layout: proc(w: *const kayan_world) -> void = {809    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w*.tables*.length, u32); ti += 1) {810        t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, ti);811        printfmt("table {} ", ti);812        kayan_print_signature(w, t*.signature);813        printfmt(": {} rows, room for {}\n", cast(t*.count, u32), cast(t*.capacity, u32));814        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {815            c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];816            if (c) {817                size: u64 = c*.size;818                printfmt("    {:-9} {:2} bytes a row, {:4} of {:4} bytes in use\n", kayan_info(w, id)*.name, cast(size, u32),819                    cast(size * t*.count, u32), cast(size * t*.capacity, u32));820            }821        }822    }823}824 825// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------826// Queries827// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------828 829// The tables a system runs over: every table whose signature has all of `all`830// and none of `none`, kept by index. Tables are only ever added, at the end of831// w.tables, so the query remembers how many it has checked and, brought up to832// date, looks at the new ones only.833kayan_query: struct = {834    all: u64;835    none: u64;836    tables: *vec<u32> in level;837    checked: u64;838}839 840// The list of matched tables lives in the world's region, so a query says841// which region it is made in.842kayan_query_init: proc(r: region level, all: u64, none: u64) -> kayan_query = {843    return { .all = all, .none = none, .tables = vec<u32>make(r, 4) };844}845 846kayan_matches: proc(signature: u64, all: u64, none: u64) -> b32 = {847    return (signature & all) == all && (signature & none) == 0;848}849 850// Check the tables made since the query last looked. With none new, this is851// one comparison, so call it before every walk.852kayan_query_update: proc(w: *const kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {853    for (ti: u64 = q*.checked; ti < w*.tables*.length; ti += 1) {854        if (kayan_matches(kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32))*.signature, q*.all, q*.none)) {855            _ = vec<u32>push(q*.tables, cast(ti, u32));856        }857    }858    q*.checked = w*.tables*.length;859}860 861// The query's i-th table.862kayan_query_table: proc(w: *const kayan_world, q: *const kayan_query, i: u64) -> *kayan_table in level = {863    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<u32>at(q*.tables, i)*);864}865 866// How many entities the query matches: the rows of its tables.867kayan_query_count: proc(w: *const kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> u64 = {868    kayan_query_update(w, q);869    n: u64 = 0;870    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q*.tables*.length; i += 1) {871        n += kayan_query_table(w, q, i)*.count;872    }873    return n;874}875 876kayan_print_query: proc(w: *const kayan_world, name: ^const char, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {877    kayan_query_update(w, q);878    printfmt("{}: all ", name);879    kayan_print_signature(w, q*.all);880    printfmt(", none ");881    kayan_print_signature(w, q*.none);882    printfmt("; tables: {}, entities: {}\n", q*.tables*.length, kayan_query_count(w, q));883    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q*.tables*.length; i += 1) {884        kayan_print_table(w, vec<u32>at(q*.tables, i)*);885    }886}887 888// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------889// Systems890// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------891 892// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------893// Commands894// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------895 896// The frame's command buffer: the commands, and the frame arena their values897// are copied into. Made at the start of each frame, in the frame region, and898// gone with it.899kayan_commands: struct = {900    heap: *kayan_heap in frame;901    list: *vec<kayan_command> in frame;902}903 904kayan_commands_make: proc(r: region frame) -> *kayan_commands in frame = {905    return new<kayan_commands>(r, { .heap = kayan_heap_make(r), .list = vec<kayan_command>make(r, 16) });906}907 908// A spawn that has been recorded and not applied. There is no entity yet, so909// this is the spawn command's place in the list; give it components with910// kayan_pending_set.911kayan_pending: struct = {912    command: u32;913}914 915kayan_defer: proc(cmds: *kayan_commands, c: kayan_command) -> u32 = {916    index: u32 = cast(cmds*.list*.length, u32);917    _ = vec<kayan_command>push(cmds*.list, c);918    return index;919}920 921// A copy of `value`, as bytes, in the frame arena. The one trusted proc of922// the command buffer: a value's bytes are a cast.923kayan_defer_value: proc<T>(h: *kayan_heap in frame, value: T) -> []u8 in frame = {924    unsafe {925        data: ^u8 = cast(memops_arena_push(h*.arena[0]&, sizeof(T), alignof(T)), ^u8);926        memcpy(data, value&, sizeof(T));927        return cast(data[0..sizeof(T)], []u8 in frame);928    }929}930 931kayan_defer_spawn: proc(cmds: *kayan_commands, signature: u64) -> kayan_pending = {932    p: kayan_pending = {};933    p.command = kayan_defer(cmds, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.spawn, .signature = signature });934    return p;935}936 937kayan_pending_set: proc<T>(cmds: *kayan_commands, p: kayan_pending, value: T) -> void = {938    _ = kayan_defer(cmds, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.add, .spawn = p.command + 1, .id = kayan_id_of<T>(),939        .value = kayan_defer_value<T>(cmds*.heap, value) });940}941 942kayan_defer_despawn: proc(cmds: *kayan_commands, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {943    _ = kayan_defer(cmds, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.despawn, .entity = e });944}945 946kayan_defer_add: proc<T>(cmds: *kayan_commands, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> void = {947    _ = kayan_defer(cmds, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.add, .entity = e, .id = kayan_id_of<T>(),948        .value = kayan_defer_value<T>(cmds*.heap, value) });949}950 951kayan_defer_remove: proc<T>(cmds: *kayan_commands, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {952    _ = kayan_defer(cmds, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.remove, .entity = e, .id = kayan_id_of<T>() });953}954 955// One applied command. The components given to a new entity are part of its956// spawn line, so they are not printed on their own.957kayan_print_command: proc(w: *const kayan_world, c: *const kayan_command, status: kayan_status) -> void = {958    if (c*.spawn != 0 && status == kayan_status.ok) {959        return;960    }961    printfmt("    {} ", c*.kind);962    if (c*.kind == kayan_command_kind.spawn) {963        kayan_print_signature(w, c*.signature);964        printfmt(" -> ");965    } else if (c*.kind != kayan_command_kind.despawn) {966        printfmt("{}, ", kayan_info(w, c*.id)*.name);967    }968    printfmt("{}:{}", c*.entity.index, c*.entity.generation);969    if (status != kayan_status.ok) {970        printfmt(": skipped, {}", status);971    }972    printfmt("\n");973}974 975// Apply the frame's commands in the order they were recorded. A command for976// an entity that died after it was recorded (despawned by an earlier command,977// most likely) does nothing, and is counted. Letting the commands go is the978// frame region's end, not a line here.979kayan_flush: proc(w: *kayan_world, cmds: *kayan_commands) -> void = {980    for (i: u64 = 0; i < cmds*.list*.length; i += 1) {981        c: *kayan_command = vec<kayan_command>at(cmds*.list, i);982        if (c*.spawn != 0) {983            c*.entity = vec<kayan_command>at(cmds*.list, cast(c*.spawn - 1, u64))*.entity;984        }985        status: kayan_status = kayan_status.ok;986        if (c*.kind == kayan_command_kind.spawn) {987            c*.entity = kayan_spawn(w, c*.signature);988        } else if (c*.kind == kayan_command_kind.despawn) {989            status = kayan_despawn(w, c*.entity);990        } else if (c*.kind == kayan_command_kind.add) {991            status = kayan_add_id(w, c*.entity, c*.id, c*.value);992        } else {993            status = kayan_remove_id(w, c*.entity, c*.id);994        }995        if (status == kayan_status.ok) {996            w*.applied += 1;997        } else {998            w*.skipped += 1;999        }1000        if (w*.trace) {1001            kayan_print_command(w, c, status);1002        }1003    }1004}1005 1006// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------1007// Systems1008// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------1009 1010// What a system gets for each table it runs on: the world, the table, the1011// frame's time step, the frame's command buffer, and `ctx`: whatever the1012// system needs beyond its own tables, here another query. It is a typed1013// pointer, not a `*void`: the checker has to know what it points at, and the1014// systems that use it test it. Every pointer names its region, so the struct1015// can be made wherever frame is open.1016kayan_iter: struct = {1017    world: *kayan_world in level;1018    table: *kayan_table in level;1019    dt: f32;1020    commands: *kayan_commands in frame;1021    ctx: option<*kayan_query in level>;1022}1023 1024kayan_system_proc: alias = *proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void;1025 1026// A system is code: a name, and the proc run on each table its query matches.1027// A C string and a proc pointer are both pointers without a region, so a1028// struct holding them is a carrier: safe code reaches it only through a1029// pointer into a region, made by a trusted proc. Neither changes after it is1030// made, so nothing is lost.1031kayan_system: struct = {1032    name: ^const char;1033    run: kayan_system_proc;1034}1035 1036kayan_system_make: proc(r: region level, name: ^const char, run: kayan_system_proc) -> *kayan_system in level = {1037    unsafe {1038        s: *kayan_system in level = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(r, sizeof(kayan_system), alignof(kayan_system)), *kayan_system in level);1039        s*.name = name;1040        s*.run = run;1041        return s;1042    }1043}1044 1045// A system in the schedule: which system, the query that finds its tables,1046// and what it has run over so far. `tables` and `rows` count the calls.1047kayan_scheduled: struct = {1048    system: *kayan_system in level;1049    query: kayan_query;1050    ctx: option<*kayan_query in level>;1051    tables: u64;1052    rows: u64;1053}1054 1055// The schedule is a list of these, in the order the frame runs them. Each1056// entry is its own allocation so a pointer to one is a pointer into level,1057// which the checker never counts as stale.1058kayan_schedule_add: proc(r: region level, systems: *vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>, name: ^const char,1059                         all: u64, none: u64, run: kayan_system_proc, ctx: option<*kayan_query in level>) -> void = {1060    _ = vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>push(systems, new<kayan_scheduled>(r, {1061        .system = kayan_system_make(r, name, run),1062        .query = kayan_query_init(r, all, none),1063        .ctx = ctx,1064    }));1065}1066 1067kayan_scheduled_at: proc(systems: *const vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>, s: u64) -> *kayan_scheduled in level = {1068    return vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>at_const(systems, s)*;1069}1070 1071// One frame: every system in order, each over every table it matches that has1072// rows, then the commands they recorded. A system sees every value the1073// systems before it wrote this frame, and no structural change until the1074// next. The caller opens the frame region and makes the buffer in it.1075kayan_progress: proc(w: *kayan_world in level, systems: *const vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>, dt: f32,1076                     cmds: *kayan_commands in frame) -> void = {1077    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems*.length; s += 1) {1078        sys: *kayan_scheduled in level = kayan_scheduled_at(systems, s);1079        kayan_query_update(w, sys*.query&);1080        for (i: u64 = 0; i < sys*.query.tables*.length; i += 1) {1081            it: kayan_iter = { .world = w, .table = kayan_query_table(w, sys*.query&, i), .dt = dt,1082                               .commands = cmds, .ctx = sys*.ctx };1083            if (it.table*.count > 0) {1084                sys*.tables += 1;1085                sys*.rows += it.table*.count;1086                sys*.system*.run(it&);1087            }1088        }1089    }1090    kayan_flush(w, cmds);1091}1092 1093kayan_print_schedule: proc(w: *const kayan_world, systems: *const vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>) -> void = {1094    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems*.length; s += 1) {1095        sys: *kayan_scheduled in level = kayan_scheduled_at(systems, s);1096        kayan_print_query(w, sys*.system*.name, sys*.query&);1097    }1098}1099 1100// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------1101// The program1102// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------1103 1104bullet_signature: proc() -> u64 = {1105    return kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>() | kayan_mask_of<damage>() | kayan_mask_of<lifetime>();1106}1107 1108spawn_bullet: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, seconds: f32) -> kayan_entity = {1109    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, bullet_signature());1110    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = 0.0 } });1111    _ = kayan_set<velocity>(w, e, { .per_second = { .x = 8.0, .y = 0.0 } });1112    _ = kayan_set<damage>(w, e, { .amount = 25.0 });1113    _ = kayan_set<lifetime>(w, e, { .seconds = seconds });1114    return e;1115}1116 1117spawn_target: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32) -> kayan_entity = {1118    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<health>());1119    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = y } });1120    _ = kayan_set<health>(w, e, { .points = 100.0, .max = 100.0 });1121    return e;1122}1123 1124// The wrong way: despawn as the loop goes. Row `row` is swap-removed, the last1125// row moves into it, and the loop moves on to row + 1. The checker lets this1126// through: the despawn takes the world, and the slice is taken again each1127// time round, so nothing it can see is stale. The row it misses is a logic1128// bug, which is the kind a loop over indices leaves you with.1129expire_now_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1130    t: *kayan_table in level = it*.table;1131    for (row: u64 = 0; row < t*.count; row += 1) {1132        ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(t);1133        es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(t);1134        if (ls[row].seconds <= 0.0) {1135            _ = kayan_despawn(it*.world, es[row]);1136        }1137    }1138}1139 1140// The right way: record the despawn. The table does not change until the1141// frame is over, so every row is looked at once.1142expire_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1143    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(it*.table);1144    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it*.table);1145    for (row: u64 = 0; row < es.length; row += 1) {1146        if (ls[row].seconds <= 0.0) {1147            kayan_defer_despawn(it*.commands, es[row]);1148        }1149    }1150}1151 1152age_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1153    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(it*.table);1154    for (row: u64 = 0; row < ls.length; row += 1) {1155        ls[row].seconds -= it*.dt;1156    }1157}1158 1159move_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1160    ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(it*.table);1161    vs: []velocity = kayan_slice<velocity>(it*.table);1162    for (row: u64 = 0; row < ps.length; row += 1) {1163        ps[row].at.x += vs[row].per_second.x * it*.dt;1164        ps[row].at.y += vs[row].per_second.y * it*.dt;1165    }1166}1167 1168// A turret whose timer is up spawns a bullet where it stands. The bullet does1169// not exist until the frame ends, so it first moves next frame.1170turret_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1171    ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(it*.table);1172    ts: []turret = kayan_slice<turret>(it*.table);1173    for (row: u64 = 0; row < ts.length; row += 1) {1174        if (ts[row].timer <= 0.0) {1175            shot: kayan_pending = kayan_defer_spawn(it*.commands, bullet_signature());1176            kayan_pending_set<position>(it*.commands, shot, ps[row]);1177            kayan_pending_set<velocity>(it*.commands, shot, { .per_second = { .x = 8.0, .y = 0.0 } });1178            kayan_pending_set<damage>(it*.commands, shot, { .amount = 25.0 });1179            kayan_pending_set<lifetime>(it*.commands, shot, { .seconds = 2.0 });1180            ts[row].timer += ts[row].cooldown;1181        }1182        ts[row].timer -= it*.dt;1183    }1184}1185 1186// A bullet within half a unit of a target hits it. The damage is a value, so1187// it is written now; the bullet's despawn is structure, so it is recorded. The1188// targets are another query, which the system gets through its ctx. During a1189// frame no table is made or moved, so walking a second query is safe.1190hit_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1191    w: *kayan_world in level = it*.world;1192    targets: option<*kayan_query in level> = it*.ctx;1193    if (!targets) {1194        return;1195    }1196    ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(it*.table);1197    ds: []damage = kayan_slice<damage>(it*.table);1198    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it*.table);1199    kayan_query_update(w, targets);1200    for (b: u64 = 0; b < es.length; b += 1) {1201        for (i: u64 = 0; i < targets*.tables*.length; i += 1) {1202            t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_query_table(w, targets, i);1203            tps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(t);1204            ths: []health = kayan_slice<health>(t);1205            for (row: u64 = 0; row < tps.length; row += 1) {1206                dx: f32 = tps[row].at.x - ps[b].at.x;1207                dy: f32 = tps[row].at.y - ps[b].at.y;1208                if (dx * dx + dy * dy < 0.25) {1209                    ths[row].points -= ds[b].amount;1210                    kayan_defer_despawn(it*.commands, es[b]);1211                }1212            }1213        }1214    }1215}1216 1217make_world: proc(r: region level) -> *kayan_world in level = {1218    w: *kayan_world in level = kayan_world_make(r);1219    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<position>(), position<>&);1220    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<velocity>(), velocity<>&);1221    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<health>(), health<>&);1222    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<damage>(), damage<>&);1223    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<lifetime>(), lifetime<>&);1224    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<turret>(), turret<>&);1225    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<burning>(), burning<>&);1226    return w;1227}1228 1229// Four bullets, three of them out of time.1230four_bullets: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {1231    _ = spawn_bullet(w, 1.0, 0.0);1232    _ = spawn_bullet(w, 2.0, 1.0);1233    _ = spawn_bullet(w, 3.0, 0.0);1234    _ = spawn_bullet(w, 4.0, 0.0);1235}1236 1237print_lifetimes: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {1238    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, kayan_table_for(w, bullet_signature()));1239    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(t);1240    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(t);1241    printfmt("    lifetimes:");1242    for (row: u64 = 0; row < t*.count; row += 1) {1243        e: kayan_entity = es[row];1244        l: lifetime = ls[row];1245        printfmt("  {}:{} {:.2}", e.index, e.generation, cast(l.seconds, f64));1246    }1247    printfmt("\n");1248}1249 1250// One frame of a world: the frame region opens, the buffer is made in it, the1251// systems run and their commands are applied, and the region ends.1252run_frame: proc(w: *kayan_world in level, systems: *const vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>, dt: f32) -> void = {1253    frame: region = {1254        kayan_progress(w, systems, dt, kayan_commands_make(frame));1255    }1256}1257 1258health_of: proc(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> f32 = {1259    h: option<*health> = kayan_get<health>(w, e);1260    return h ? h*.points : 0.0;1261}1262 1263main: proc() -> i32 = {1264    level: region = {1265        lifetime_only: u64 = kayan_mask_of<lifetime>();1266 1267        printfmt("1. an expire system that despawns as it goes\n");1268        a: *kayan_world in level = make_world(level);1269        four_bullets(a);1270        print_lifetimes(a);1271        wrong: *vec<*kayan_scheduled in level> in level = vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>make(level, 1);1272        kayan_schedule_add(level, wrong, "expire", lifetime_only, 0, expire_now_system, null);1273        run_frame(a, wrong, 0.25);1274        printfmt("after one frame:\n");1275        print_lifetimes(a);1276        printfmt("kayan_verify: {} problems. The world is fine; the loop missed one.\n", kayan_verify(a));1277 1278        printfmt("\n2. an expire system that records despawns\n");1279        b: *kayan_world in level = make_world(level);1280        b*.trace = true;1281        four_bullets(b);1282        print_lifetimes(b);1283        right: *vec<*kayan_scheduled in level> in level = vec<*kayan_scheduled in level>make(level, 1);1284 Build an ECS · part 3, systems · 3.4

A game

ecs/src/3.systems/3.4.game/game.rin

In the dojo: this chapter puts the building blocks together; the dojo has each one on its own, to watch and to practise.

Everything together. Three lanes, a turret at the left end of each, and drones coming from the right in waves:

  • a turret fires down its lane while there's a drone in it;
  • a bullet that reaches a drone damages it;
  • a drone below half health catches fire;
  • a drone with no health left is destroyed;
  • a drone that gets to the left end has reached the base.

The top of the file is kayan, as 3.3 left it, with one type changed: ctx now points at the game. The game is the bottom: components, kernels, systems, a schedule and a level script. Every rule of the game is a system over a query. Every structural change a system makes is a command.

The pieces

The components are the same seven from 2.1. A drone is a signature:

drone_signature: proc() -> u64 = {
    return kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>() | kayan_mask_of<health>();
}

A burning drone is that plus burning, which puts it in another table. There is no drone type anywhere in the program. A drone is whatever lives in a table with these columns.

What the systems share (the drones query, the clock, the score) is one struct, handed to the systems that need it through ctx:

game: struct = {
    drones: kayan_query;
    time: f32;
    fired: u32;
    hits: u32;
    fires: u32;
    kills: u32;
    breaches: u32;
    came: u32;
}

It lives in level memory, beside the world, so an iterator can hold it:

        g: *game in level = new<game>(level, {
            .drones = kayan_query_init(level, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<health>(), 0),
        });

Not every system has a game to look at, so the iterator's field is an option<*game in level>, and a system that wants it starts by testing it:

ignite_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {
    g: option<*game in level> = it*.ctx;
    if (!g) {
        return;
    }

The schedule

        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "turret", shooting, 0, turret_system, g);
        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "age", kayan_mask_of<lifetime>(), 0, age_system, null);
        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "expire", kayan_mask_of<lifetime>(), 0, expire_system, null);
        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "move", movers, 0, move_system, null);
        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "hit", bullets, 0, hit_system, g);
        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "ignite", kayan_mask_of<health>(), kayan_mask_of<burning>(), ignite_system, g);
        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "burn", kayan_mask_of<health>() | kayan_mask_of<burning>(), 0, burn_system, null);
        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "die", kayan_mask_of<health>(), 0, die_system, g);
        kayan_schedule_add(level, systems, "breach", kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<health>(), 0, breach_system, g);

Read it as the frame, top to bottom. Each line's position is a data-flow decision (3.2):

  • move before hit: bullets hit where they are, not where they were.
  • hit before ignite, burn and die: a drone takes damage, catches fire and is destroyed in the same frame its health drops.
  • die before breach: only a drone that survived the frame can reach the base. breach also checks health > 0 itself, because both run in the same frame and die's despawn hasn't been applied yet.
  • ignite has none {burning}: a drone catches fire once. The add is a command, so next frame it's in the burning table and the query no longer matches it.

The rules

Each one is a few lines. The ones that only change values call kernels, with the noalias promise from 3.2 kept right there at the call: a health column and a burning column can't overlap.

burn_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {
    unsafe { burn(kayan_slice<health>(it*.table), kayan_slice<burning>(it*.table), it*.dt); }
}

The ones that change structure record commands:

        if (hs[row].points < 0.5 * hs[row].max && hs[row].points > 0.0) {
            kayan_defer_add<burning>(it*.commands, es[row], { .per_second = 10.0 });
            g*.fires += 1;
        }

The turret is the most involved. It asks the drones query whether anything is ahead of it in its lane, then spawns a bullet with a pending spawn (3.3):

        if (ts[row].timer <= 0.0 && drone_ahead(it*.world, g, ps[row].at.x, ps[row].at.y)) {

hit is 3.3's hit system, with one extra thought about speed. A bullet moves a unit a frame and a fast drone a quarter, so they close by at most 1.25 a frame. A hit window of ±0.75 is 1.5 wide, so no bullet can pass through a drone between two frames:

                if (dx * dx < 0.5625 && dy * dy < 0.25) {

The level

The waves aren't a system. They're the level script, and it runs between frames, in the game loop, where spawning directly is safe:

        for (frame_no: u32 = 0; frame_no < frames; frame_no += 1) {
            g*.time = cast(frame_no, f32) * dt;
            if (frame_no % 32 == 0 && frame_no / 32 < 8) {
                send_wave(w, g, frame_no / 32);
            }
            run_frame(w, systems, dt);
            problems += kayan_verify(w);

run_frame opens the frame region and closes it again, 512 times, so every command and every copied value from the whole game ends with the frame that recorded it. Level memory holds what lasts.

kayan_verify runs after every frame: 512 checks of Part 1's invariant over the whole world.

Drawing by table

The picture of the lanes walks a query of everything with a position. What an entity is drawn as comes from its table's signature, decided once per table, not per entity:

glyph_of: proc(signature: u64) -> c8 = {
    if ((signature & kayan_mask_of<turret>()) != 0) {
        return 'T';
    }
    if ((signature & kayan_mask_of<burning>()) != 0) {
        return '*';
    }
    if ((signature & kayan_mask_of<health>()) != 0) {
        return 'd';
    }
    return '-';
}

In an OOP engine this would be a virtual draw() per object. Here it's a property of a table, and the inner loop is a plain loop over positions.

Exact on purpose

Every speed and time step is a power of two: dt is 1/16, drones move 2 or 4 units a second, bullets 16, fire burns 10 a second (0.625 a frame). So every position, health and timer is exactly representable, and no rounding ever happens. That's why a Debug build, a Release build, gcc, clang and a CPU that fuses multiply-adds all print the same game. Real games give that up for nicer numbers. Rounding differences usually don't matter, but they do the day you want a replay or a lockstep network game.

What you built

Part 1  entities       handles, generations, slots, swap-remove, kayan_verify
Part 2  components     ids, columns, tables, archetypes, typed access,
                       moving between tables, the archetype graph, reflection
Part 3  systems        queries, kernels and schedules, commands, a game

That's a working archetype ECS, about 790 lines of kayan without comments. It's the design flecs is built on (tables, the archetype graph, cached queries, command buffers), and Bevy and Unity DOTS are close cousins, minus their years of features.

And it's memory safe, with very little left on trust. Here's all of it. Kayan has eight unsafe { } blocks, each a place where bytes meet types or where memory gets its region: 3.1's six, plus kayan_system_make for the proc pointers (3.2) and kayan_defer_value for a value's bytes (3.3). The game adds three noalias kernels, each called from a one-line unsafe { } that keeps its promise. Everything else is checked, and that's the rest of the file: the world, the tables, the queries, the commands, and every other rule of the game. And the blocks that turn bytes into types don't take the checked code's word for anything: 2.2's rule holds to the end, so a mistake up here stops the game or gives it wrong numbers.

The safety and the data-oriented design turned out to want the same things. Memory that ends all at once is what a level and a frame already are. Handles, not pointers, were already how an ECS names things. Commands were already how it keeps tables still while a system walks them. Very little of this design exists only to satisfy the checker.

Things worth adding next, roughly in order of how much they teach:

  • Relationships: child_of(parent) as a component, flecs' big idea.
  • Change detection: a per-column version number, so a system can skip tables nothing wrote to.
  • Parallel systems: systems that don't write what others read can run at the same time. The schedule already holds what you need to decide that.
  • Removing empty tables, and the queries' table lists with them.
  • Serialization: the reflect records already describe every byte; write the tables out and read them back.

Try

  1. Add a fourth lane. What changes? (Only the level: lanes, the picture.)
  2. Make bullets pierce: they don't despawn on a hit, but each drone can only be hit by a bullet once. Where does "once" live? (A component on the bullet? On the drone?)
  3. Add a shield component that absorbs the next hit, then removes itself. Which systems change?
  4. Print kayan_inspect of a drone the frame it catches fire.

The level script that sends the waves16// runs between frames, where spawning directly is safe.17//18// Every speed and time step is a power of two, so the arithmetic is exact and19// a Debug and a Release build print the same game.20//21// The game's state is a `game` in level memory, and the systems reach it22// through the typed `ctx` on their iterator. The rest is checked.25 26import "std/print.rin"27import "std/vec.rin"28import "std/hashmap.rin"29import "std/slice.rin"30 31level: region;32frame: region in level;33 34vec2: struct = {35    x: f32;36    y: f32;37}38 39position: struct = { at: vec2; }40velocity: struct = { per_second: vec2; }41health: struct = { points: f32; max: f32; }42damage: struct = { amount: f32; }43lifetime: struct = { seconds: f32; }44// A field tagged "hidden" is bookkeeping the inspector does not show.45turret: struct = { cooldown: f32; timer: f32 @ "hidden"; }46burning: struct = { per_second: f32; }47 48component: enum = {49    position,50    velocity,51    health,52    damage,53    lifetime,54    turret,55    burning,56}57 58component_of: proc<position>() -> component = { return component.position; }59component_of: proc<velocity>() -> component = { return component.velocity; }60component_of: proc<health>() -> component = { return component.health; }61component_of: proc<damage>() -> component = { return component.damage; }62component_of: proc<lifetime>() -> component = { return component.lifetime; }63component_of: proc<turret>() -> component = { return component.turret; }64component_of: proc<burning>() -> component = { return component.burning; }65 66// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------67// Entities (Part 1)68// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------69 70kayan_entity: struct = {71    index: u32;72    generation: u32;73}74 75// `missing`: the entity is alive but has no such component.76kayan_status: enum[must_use] = {77    ok,78    dead,79    missing,80}81 82// Where an entity lives: which table, and which row of it.83kayan_slot: struct = {84    generation: u32;85    table: u32;86    row: u32;87}88 89// A structural change recorded during a frame and applied after it (3.3).90// `entity` is who it applies to; a spawn's is filled in when it is applied. An91// add to an entity spawned in the same frame has no entity to name yet, so it92// names its spawn instead: `spawn` is that command's index plus one. The93// value's bytes are frame memory, like the command itself.94kayan_command_kind: enum = {95    spawn,96    despawn,97    add,98    remove,99}100 101kayan_command: struct = {102    kind: kayan_command_kind;103    entity: kayan_entity;104    spawn: u32;105    id: u32;106    signature: u64;107    value: []u8 in frame;108}109 110// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------111// The byte core: columns (2.2), and the region they grow into112// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------113 114// The region's arena, kept where the trusted procs can reach it: the world115// remembers where it was made, as a vec does, so nothing above this layer116// hands an arena around.117kayan_heap: struct = {118    arena: ^memops_arena;119}120 121kayan_heap_make: proc(r: region R) -> *kayan_heap in R = {122    unsafe {123        h: *kayan_heap in R = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(r, sizeof(kayan_heap), alignof(kayan_heap)), *kayan_heap in R);124        h*.arena = r;125        return h;126    }127}128 129// One component's values for every row of a table, as bytes: `size` of them130// a row, `capacity` rows allocated (the table knows how many are in use).131kayan_column: struct = {132    data: []u8 in level;133    size: u64;134    align: u64;135}136 137kayan_column_make: proc(h: *kayan_heap in level, info: *const reflect in permanent) -> *kayan_column in level = {138    unsafe {139        c: *kayan_column in level = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(h*.arena[0]&, sizeof(kayan_column), alignof(kayan_column)), *kayan_column in level);140        c*.size = info*.size;141        c*.align = info*.align;142        return c;143    }144}145 146// Room for `capacity` rows, the first `count` copied over. The old storage is147// left in the region: a slice taken before the grow still points at valid148// memory, and stale values.149kayan_column_grow: proc(h: *kayan_heap, c: *kayan_column, count: u64, capacity: u64) -> void = {150    unsafe {151        raw: ^u8 = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(h*.arena[0]&, c*.size * capacity, c*.align), ^u8);152        bytes: []u8 in level = cast(raw[0..c*.size * capacity], []u8 in level);153        // Slicing checks both ends: a count past either block stops the program.154        kept: u64 = c*.size * count;155        slice<u8>copy(bytes[0..kept], c*.data[0..kept]);156        c*.data = bytes;157    }158}159 160// One row's bytes, bounds-checked like any slice.161kayan_column_bytes: proc(c: *kayan_column, row: u64) -> []u8 in level = {162    return c*.data[row * c*.size..(row + 1) * c*.size];163}164 165// The typed view: the column's first `count` rows as `[]T`. This is the one166// place bytes become a type, so it takes nothing on trust. T must be the167// column's size, and plain data: any bytes are then a valid T, so reading the168// wrong type gives wrong numbers, never a bad pointer. The rows must fit, which169// the slice knows and no field can lie about, and the bytes must be aligned for170// T. The view is `[]T in level`: the bytes are in the region, so the view is171// good memory for as long as the region is. After the column grows it is the172// old block, still readable, no longer the column: take the view again.173kayan_column_slice: proc<T>(c: *const kayan_column, count: u64) -> []T in level = {174    if (c*.size != sizeof(T)) {175        printfmt("kayan: a column of {}-byte rows read as a {}-byte type\n", c*.size, sizeof(T));176        exit(1);177    }178    if (!reflect_is_plain(T<>&)) {179        printfmt("kayan: a column holds plain data, and this {}-byte type is not\n", sizeof(T));180        exit(1);181    }182    if (count > c*.data.length / sizeof(T)) {183        printfmt("kayan: a view of {} rows on a column with room for {}\n", count, c*.data.length / sizeof(T));184        exit(1);185    }186    unsafe {187        if (cast(c*.data.data, usize) % alignof(T) != 0) {188            printfmt("kayan: a column's bytes are not aligned to {}\n", alignof(T));189            exit(1);190        }191        raw: ^T = cast(c*.data.data, ^T);192        return cast(raw[0..count], []T in level);193    }194}195 196// Copying and zeroing a row are loops over the row's bytes: checked code.197kayan_column_copy_row: proc(c: *kayan_column, to: u64, from: u64) -> void = {198    dst: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(c, to);199    src: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(c, from);200    for (i: u64 = 0; i < dst.length; i += 1) {201        dst[i] = src[i];202    }203}204 205kayan_column_zero_row: proc(c: *kayan_column, row: u64) -> void = {206    bytes: []u8 = kayan_column_bytes(c, row);207    for (i: u64 = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1) {208        bytes[i] = 0;209    }210}211 212// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------213// The table214// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------215 216// `columns[id]` is a column when the signature has bit `id`, and null217// otherwise. Count and capacity are the table's, shared by its columns, so218// they can never disagree; `entities` grows on its own and always has `count`219// rows.220//221// The edges: `add_edges[id]` is the table this one's entities move to when222// they gain component `id`, and `remove_edges[id]` when they lose it. Each is223// the table's index plus one, so 0, which a new table starts with, means "not224// known yet".225kayan_table: struct = {226    signature: u64;227    count: u64;228    capacity: u64;229    entities: *vec<kayan_entity> in level;230    columns: [64]option<*kayan_column in level>;231    add_edges: [64]u32;232    remove_edges: [64]u32;233}234 235// A zeroed table in the region, with an empty entities vec: the world fills236// in the signature and the columns.237kayan_table_new: proc(h: *kayan_heap in level) -> *kayan_table in level = {238    unsafe {239        t: *kayan_table in level = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(h*.arena[0]&, sizeof(kayan_table), alignof(kayan_table)), *kayan_table in level);240        v: *vec<kayan_entity> in level = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(h*.arena[0]&, sizeof(vec<kayan_entity>), alignof(vec<kayan_entity>)), *vec<kayan_entity> in level);241        v*.arena = h*.arena;242        t*.entities = v;243        return t;244    }245}246 247// The world: the registry, the slots and free list, and every table, with a248// map from signature to table index so finding one is a lookup, not a search.249// Tables are referred to by index, so a table can be named in a slot; each250// table is its own allocation, so a pointer to one stays good when the next251// is made.252kayan_world: struct = {253    heap: *kayan_heap in level;254    infos: [64]option<*const reflect in permanent>;255    component_count: u32;256    tables: *vec<*kayan_table in level> in level;257    by_signature: *hashmap<u64, u32> in level;258    slots: *vec<kayan_slot> in level;259    free: *vec<u32> in level;260    live: u64;261    // What the flushes did, and whether to print each command as it is applied.262    applied: u64;263    skipped: u64;264    trace: b32;265}266 267kayan_bit: proc(id: u32) -> u64 = {268    return 1'u64 shl cast(id, u64);269}270 271kayan_id_of: proc<T>() -> u32 = {272    return cast(component_of<T>(), u32);273}274 275kayan_mask_of: proc<T>() -> u64 = {276    return kayan_bit(kayan_id_of<T>());277}278 279// The reflect records live for the whole program, so `permanent` is their280// region and the world may keep them.281kayan_register: proc(w: *kayan_world, id: u32, info: *const reflect in permanent) -> void = {282    if (id >= 64) {283        printfmt("kayan: component id {} is past the 64 a signature can hold\n", id);284        exit(1);285    }286    w*.infos[id] = info;287    if (id + 1 > w*.component_count) {288        w*.component_count = id + 1;289    }290}291 292// A registered component's record. The checker needs the null test; the293// return after exit is never reached.294kayan_info: proc(w: *const kayan_world, id: u32) -> *const reflect in permanent = {295    info: option<*const reflect in permanent> = w*.infos[id];296    if (info) {297        return info;298    }299    printfmt("kayan: component {} was never registered\n", id);300    exit(1);301    return kayan_entity<>&;302}303 304kayan_table_has: proc(t: *const kayan_table, id: u32) -> b32 = {305    return (t*.signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0;306}307 308// A table for a signature: one empty column per component in it, sized from309// the registry. Every component in the signature must be registered.310kayan_table_make: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> *kayan_table in level = {311    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_new(w*.heap);312    t*.signature = signature;313    for (id: u32 = 0; id < 64; id += 1) {314        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {315            if (id >= w*.component_count) {316                printfmt("kayan: signature {} uses component {}, which was never registered\n", signature, id);317                exit(1);318            }319            t*.columns[id] = kayan_column_make(w*.heap, kayan_info(w, id));320        }321    }322    return t;323}324 325// Double the room in every column at once.326kayan_table_grow: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table) -> void = {327    capacity: u64 = t*.capacity == 0 ? 4 : t*.capacity * 2;328    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {329        c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];330        if (c) {331            kayan_column_grow(w*.heap, c, t*.count, capacity);332        }333    }334    t*.capacity = capacity;335}336 337// A new row at the end, owned by `e`, with every component zeroed.338kayan_table_add_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {339    if (t*.count == t*.capacity) {340        kayan_table_grow(w, t);341    }342    row: u64 = t*.count;343    t*.count += 1;344    _ = vec<kayan_entity>push(t*.entities, e);345    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {346        c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];347        if (c) {348            kayan_column_zero_row(c, row);349        }350    }351    return row;352}353 354// Who owns each of the table's rows. It only reads, and the checker sees that,355// so a system holds this and two or three columns of one table at once.356kayan_entities: proc(t: *const kayan_table) -> []kayan_entity in level = {357    return vec<kayan_entity>items(t*.entities);358}359 360// 1.4's swap-remove, for every column: the last row is copied over `row`, and361// the slot of the entity that owned the last row is told where it went.362kayan_table_remove_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, row: u64) -> void = {363    last: u64 = t*.count - 1;364    if (row != last) {365        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {366            c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];367            if (c) {368                kayan_column_copy_row(c, row, last);369            }370        }371        moved: kayan_entity = vec<kayan_entity>at(t*.entities, last)*;372        vec<kayan_entity>at(t*.entities, row)* = moved;373        vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(moved.index, u64))*.row = cast(row, u32);374    }375    _ = vec<kayan_entity>pop(t*.entities);376    t*.count = last;377}378 379// The typed view of one of the table's columns: T's rows, all of them in use.380// Asking for a component the table does not have is a bug, so it stops. The381// slice is good memory for as long as the region, but when the table grows it is382// the old block, no longer the column: take it again, and 3.3 makes that a rule.383kayan_slice: proc<T>(t: *const kayan_table) -> []T in level = {384    id: u32 = kayan_id_of<T>();385    c: option<*kayan_column in level> = t*.columns[id];386    if (!c) {387        printfmt("kayan: the table has no column for component {}\n", id);388        exit(1);389    }390    return kayan_column_slice<T>(c, t*.count);391}392 393kayan_table_at: proc(w: *const kayan_world, index: u32) -> *kayan_table in level = {394    return vec<*kayan_table in level>at(w*.tables, cast(index, u64))*;395}396 397// The table for a signature: found if it exists, made if it does not. This is398// where archetypes come from.399kayan_table_for: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> u32 = {400    found: option<*u32> = hashmap<u64, u32>get(w*.by_signature, signature);401    if (found) {402        return found*;403    }404    index: u32 = cast(w*.tables*.length, u32);405    _ = vec<*kayan_table in level>push(w*.tables, kayan_table_make(w, signature));406    _ = hashmap<u64, u32>set(w*.by_signature, signature, index);407    return index;408}409 410// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------411// The world412// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------413 414kayan_world_make: proc(r: region level) -> *kayan_world in level = {415    return new<kayan_world>(r, {416        .heap = kayan_heap_make(r),417        .tables = vec<*kayan_table in level>make(r, 8),418        .by_signature = hashmap<u64, u32>make(r),419        .slots = vec<kayan_slot>make(r, 64),420        .free = vec<u32>make(r, 16),421    });422}423 424kayan_alive: proc(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {425    if (cast(e.index, u64) >= w*.slots*.length) {426        return false;427    }428    return vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.generation == e.generation;429}430 431// A new entity with the components in `signature`, all zeroed, in the table432// for that signature.433kayan_spawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> kayan_entity = {434    e: kayan_entity = {};435    if (w*.free*.length > 0) {436        e.index = vec<u32>pop(w*.free);437    } else {438        e.index = cast(w*.slots*.length, u32);439        _ = vec<kayan_slot>push(w*.slots, { .generation = 1 });440    }441    e.generation = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64))*.generation;442    table_index: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, signature);443    t: *kayan_table in level = kayan_table_at(w, table_index);444    row: u64 = kayan_table_add_row(w, t, e);445    // The slot is taken after the calls that change the world: a pointer into446    // `slots` from before them may be stale, and the checker says so.447    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));448    slot*.table = table_index;449    slot*.row = cast(row, u32);450    w*.live += 1;451    return e;452}453 454kayan_despawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {455    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {456        return kayan_status.dead;457    }458    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));459    table: u32 = slot*.table;460    row: u32 = slot*.row;461    kayan_table_remove_row(w, kayan_table_at(w, table), cast(row, u64));462    slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, cast(e.index, u64));463    slot*.generation += 1;464    _ = vec<u32>push(w*.free, e.index);465    w*.live -= 1;466    return kayan_status.ok;467}468 469// The components a live entity has: its table's signature. 0 for a dead one.470kayan_signature: proc(w: *const kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {471    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {472        return 0;473    }474    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots, ---------------------------------------------------------------------------480 481// The table an entity of table `from` moves to when it gains component `id`.482// The first time, it is found by signature, which can make the table; the483// answer is written on both tables, as from's add edge and the destination's484// remove edge, so neither direction is looked up again.485kayan_table_with: kayan_table_for(w, kayan_table_at(w, from)*.signature | kayan_bit(id));491    kayan_table_at(w, from)*.add_edges[id] = to + 1;492    kayan_table_at(w, to)*.remove_edges[id] = from + 1;493    return
